Fact: The International Boxing Association is an international sporting organization that sanctions amateur boxing.
It was recognized by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) as the governing body for Olympic boxing until 2019, when its recognition was suspended.
In 2023, the IOC stripped the IBA of recognition entirely, making it the only international sports organization to have been expelled from the Olympics.

Among the reasons for this were persistent allegations of corruption, increasing involvement with Russian financial interests including Gazprom, and moving much of the organization’s operations into Russia.
Fact: For 2024, the IOC itself is the governing body for Olympic boxing.
Fact: Imane Khelif competed in IBA sanctioned World Championships for a number of years prior to 2023, winning a silver medal in 2022.
There was no controversy about her participation in these events.
Fact: In 2023, Imane Khelif defeated a Russian boxer, Amineva Azalia, to secure a spot in the quarterfinal round of the competition.
Unsubstantiated speculation: There has been much speculation that her disqualification was actually on the basis of testosterone levels, but IBA has pushed back on those claims.
In any case, such a disqualification would be temporary and a disqualified athlete would be allowed to compete in future events if their testosterone level was lower at that event.
Unsubstantiated speculation: There has also been much speculation about her having an unusual genetic condition that would result in her having a female reproductive system and XY chromosomes.
This is possible, but there is no evidence supporting the speculation.
Fact: In 2024, the IOC has publicly stated that Khelif meets its requirements for participation.
